meta.title: AstanaTechCup {year} — National Robotics & Tech Championship of Kazakhstan
meta.description: The 3rd national technology championship of Kazakhstan. Robotics, drones, programming and esports. 2,500 participants, 720 teams. Winners represent Kazakhstan at the international RobotChallenge.
meta.ogAlt: AstanaTechCup — national robotics championship of Kazakhstan

hero.subtitle: AstanaTechCup is Kazakhstan's national technology championship for school and university students. Six disciplines, teams from every region of the country, and a place at the international RobotChallenge for the winners.

flagship.title: RoboSumo
flagship.lead: Two robots. A ring less than a metre across. Whoever leaves it first loses.
flagship.body: The most spectacular discipline of the championship, and the easiest one for a newcomer to grasp: the rules take a minute to explain, and winning comes down to engineering rather than budget. Several weight and size classes run in parallel, from simple builds for beginners to autonomous machines fielded by experienced teams.
flagship.point1Body: Push your opponent out of the ring. Everything else is regulation detail.
flagship.point2Body: Size and weight classes mean a first-timer and a seasoned team never meet in the same bracket.
flagship.point3Body: Bouts run over several rounds and draw the largest audience of the championship.
flagship.provisionalNote: Age categories, team size and weight classes will be confirmed in the regulations.

disciplines.title: Six disciplines — pick yours
disciplines.subtitle: Each discipline has its own age categories and team size. Full technical requirements are in the championship regulations.
disciplines.regulationsMissing: The regulations will be published before entries open.

robosumo.name: RoboSumo
robosumo.description: Two robots face off in a circular ring. The one that pushes its opponent out wins. Several weight and size classes.

vex.name: VEX
vex.description: The international VEX Robotics platform: build, program and drive a robot as a team to complete this season's game challenges.

lego.name: LEGO
lego.description: Building and programming robots on the LEGO platform. The best starting point for younger students and anyone trying competition for the first time.

arduino.name: Arduino
arduino.description: Building microcontroller devices: your own circuit, soldering, sensors and code. For anyone who wants to understand how it all works underneath.

drones.name: Drones
drones.description: Course racing, precision piloting and autonomous flight tasks. Reaction speed plus solid engineering on the airframe.

esports.name: Esports
esports.description: Team esports tournaments with a group stage and play-offs. The largest teams in the championship.

journey.title: From entry to podium — seven steps
journey.subtitle: No hidden stages. You always know what comes next and what to prepare.

application.title: Entry
application.body: Register your team in your chosen discipline and pay the entry fee. It takes a few minutes.

confirmation.title: Confirmation
confirmation.body: The organising committee checks your team's details and emails you confirmation along with the discipline regulations.

preparation.title: Preparation
preparation.body: Build your robot and write your program to the regulations. Answers to technical questions and breakdowns of previous seasons are published before the start.

techCheck.title: Technical inspection
techCheck.body: On site, judges check your robot against the regulations: dimensions, weight, safety. Minor issues can be fixed within a grace period.

qualification.title: Qualifying
qualification.body: Qualifying runs and bouts within your category. The result sets your position in the bracket.

final.title: Final
final.body: Decisive bouts in every category, in front of the hall and the judging panel.

awards.title: Awards
awards.body: Diplomas, medals and prizes. The strongest robotics teams get their shot at a place in Beijing.

prizes.title: The top prize isn't a trophy
prizes.lead: Winners of the robotics disciplines earn the chance to represent Kazakhstan at the international RobotChallenge.
prizes.internationalBody: The international stage takes place in Beijing. For championship teams it is a direct route to the world stage and opponents from dozens of countries.

medals.title: Medals and trophies
medals.body: For the podium in every category of every discipline.

diplomas.title: Diplomas and certificates
diplomas.body: A certificate for every participant, and letters of commendation for the schools and clubs that prepared teams.

special.title: Special awards
special.body: Separate prizes for unconventional engineering and standout results.

valuable.title: Prizes
valuable.body: Winners and runners-up receive commemorative and valuable prizes from the organisers and partners.

audiences.title: Choose your role
audiences.subtitle: The championship is more than the teams on the floor. Find the route that fits you.

participant.title: Competitor

parent.title: Parent
parent.body: Want to enter your child but not sure where to start? Answers to the common questions about cost, travel and the level required.

teacher.title: Teacher or club

spectator.title: Spectator

volunteer.title: Volunteer

faq.title: Answered in advance
faq.subtitle: The things competitors, parents and teachers ask us most.

cost.q: What does it cost to take part?
cost.a: The entry fee is {amount} {currency} per team, not per person. It covers participation in every stage of your chosen discipline, certificates and access to the venue. Everything else — travel, accommodation and building your robot — the team plans for itself.

travel.q: We're from another region. How do we get there?
travel.a: The championship is held in Astana. Teams usually plan to arrive the day before so they can get through technical inspection without rushing. The exact venue address, directions and recommended arrival time are sent to confirmed teams along with the regulations.

accommodation.q: Is there help with accommodation for teams from out of town?
accommodation.a: Accommodation is being confirmed with the organising committee. Mention it when you submit your entry, with your city and the number of people, and we'll suggest options near the venue and tell you whether any special rates apply for teams.

skillLevel.q: We've never competed before. Should we still enter?
skillLevel.a: Yes. The championship is open to teams at any level, from students building their first robot to experienced university teams. Every discipline has age categories, and RoboSumo adds weight classes on top, so beginners never face champions.

rules.q: Where can we read the rules and technical requirements?
rules.a: The full regulations are published before entries open and can be downloaded from this page. They cover robot dimensions and weight, permitted components, the format of bouts, and the judging criteria for each discipline.

selection.q: How are teams selected for the international stage?
selection.a: Places at RobotChallenge go to the strongest robotics teams based on the final. The selection criteria and the number of places are published in the regulations before the championship begins — nothing is decided behind closed doors afterwards.

teamChanges.q: Can we change the team line-up after entering?
teamChanges.a: Yes. Until entries close, changes are made by writing to the organising committee with your reference. After the deadline, substitutions are considered individually and only for good reason.

refund.q: What if our team can't make it?
refund.a: Let the organising committee know as early as you can, quoting your reference. The refund terms for the entry fee, and whether the place can be passed to another team from your organisation, are set out in the terms of participation.

equipment.q: Do we need to bring our own equipment?
equipment.a: Yes. Teams bring their own robot, tools and spare parts. There is a pit area at the venue with workbenches and power; what the organiser provides is listed in each discipline's regulations.

deadline.a: {date}, inclusive. We'd suggest not leaving it late: places in some categories are limited, and no entries are accepted after the deadline.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what personal data is processed when you enter the AstanaTechCup championship, why, and how long it is kept.
privacy.draftNotice: Draft. This document was prepared as a starting point and must be reviewed by the organiser's legal counsel before publication, including for compliance with the Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V on personal data and its protection.
privacy.s1Body: The data controller is the championship organiser, {organizer}. Contact details for data protection enquiries are published in the Contact section.
privacy.s2Body: When you submit an entry: the team and organisation name, region and city, the names and ages of team members, and the contact person's name, email, phone number and note. When you pay the entry fee, payment details are handled by the payment provider — this site neither receives nor stores card details.
privacy.s3Body: To register your team and admit it to the competition, to confirm the entry and stay in touch, to produce results and award documents, and to keep the service secure and free from abuse.
privacy.s4Body: The championship's main audience is schoolchildren. Data about participants under 18 is submitted by a legal guardian or with their consent; confirming this is a mandatory condition of entry.
privacy.s5Body: Entry data is retained for the duration of the championship and the reporting period that follows, after which it is deleted or anonymised. Specific periods are set out in the controller's internal policy.
privacy.s6Body: Data is never sold, and never passed to third parties for advertising. Limited access is held by the service providers needed to run the site: hosting, email delivery, the payment provider and the bot-protection service.
privacy.s7Body: You may request a copy of your data, ask for it to be corrected or deleted, and withdraw your consent to processing. Contact the organising committee quoting your entry reference.
privacy.s8Body: Essential cookies keep the registration form working and protect against request forgery. Analytics cookies are set only after explicit consent and can be declined without losing any site functionality.
privacy.s9Body: Data is transmitted over an encrypted connection, access to it is restricted, and actions on entries are logged. Personal data is never written to service logs in the clear.

terms.title: Terms of participation
terms.draftNotice: Draft. This document was prepared as a starting point and must be reviewed by the organiser's legal counsel and aligned with the official competition regulations.
terms.s1Body: These terms govern entry to and participation in the AstanaTechCup national technology championship. The organiser is {organizer}; the co-organiser is {coOrganizer}.
terms.s2Body: Teams of school and university students who meet the age categories of their chosen discipline may take part. Age limits and maximum team size are stated in each discipline's description and checked when the entry is submitted.
terms.s3Body: Entries are submitted through the form on this site up to and including {deadline}. An entry is accepted once the organising committee has confirmed it and the entry fee has been received.
terms.s4Body: The fee is {amount} {currency} per team, paid through the payment provider's secure page. Refund terms are set by the competition regulations; a team withdrawing should notify the organising committee in good time.
terms.s5Body: Participants must follow their discipline's regulations. Robots undergo a technical inspection against the requirements for dimensions, weight and safety. Non-compliance may result in exclusion until the issues are resolved.
terms.s6Body: Results are determined by the judging panel according to the criteria published in the regulations. The procedure for lodging and hearing appeals is set out in the competition regulations.
terms.s7Body: Photography and filming take place at the venue. Consent to publish material featuring your team is requested separately and has no bearing on admission to the competition.
terms.s8Body: The organiser may adjust the dates, venue and regulations, giving registered teams timely notice through the contact details provided in their entry.
